name: SEOvault AI – Automated AI SEO – Schema, Sitemap & llms.txt
author: seovaultai

sections.description:
SEOvault AI automatically generates SEO titles and meta descriptions in WordPress. Use automatic mode to handle routine SEO tasks, switch to manual mode to edit the details yourself, or disable individual features when another tool handles them.

Free features

  • Search and social previews. Set focus keywords, canonical URLs, robots directives, and Open Graph and X Card metadata.
  • Structured data and sitemaps. Add JSON-LD schema and publish XML sitemaps that exclude content marked noindex.
  • Local SEO and WooCommerce. Add business information and generate product schema when WooCommerce is active.
  • Redirects and 404 monitoring. Find broken URLs, create redirects, and customize how visitors recover from missing pages.
  • Crawler tools. Publish llms.txt, manage robots.txt rules, and see which AI crawlers visit your site.
  • SEO data import. Bring over existing metadata from supported SEO plugins.

The free plugin works directly in WordPress. Connect to the optional SEOvault AI web app for cloud-based AI and bulk workflows.

SEOvault AI documentation

External services

The free plugin runs locally. The following requests occur when an administrator connects, configures, enables, or uses the relevant feature.

SEOvault AI web app

The optional web app provides cloud-based AI, bulk site management, reports, and content workflows. After an administrator connects with a site key, authorized actions can read or update WordPress content, SEO metadata, media, schema, redirects, robots.txt, llms.txt, and other plugin settings. The plugin does not upload posts to the web app automatically in the background.

When an authorized action supplies a public image URL and the image is not already local, the WordPress server requests the image from that host and saves it to the Media Library. The host receives the site’s server IP address and standard HTTP request headers. The request carries no WordPress post content. The image provider’s terms and privacy policy depend on the supplied URL.

SEOvault AI web app | Terms of Service | Privacy Policy

SEOvault AI Pro licensing

When an administrator activates a license in the separate Pro plugin, Pro contacts SEOvault AI to verify entitlements. It can also refresh activation status and download authorized updates. The free plugin works without a license.

SEOvault AI Pro | Terms of Service | Privacy Policy

IndexNow

When enabled, IndexNow receives public URLs that are published, updated, or manually submitted, along with the site host and verification key. This notifies participating search engines that the URLs changed.

IndexNow | Terms and privacy information

Google Analytics

When an administrator enables Google Analytics and enters a Measurement ID, eligible public pages load Google tag code from googletagmanager.com. Visitors’ browsers send page, device, network, and interaction data to Google according to the site’s Analytics configuration. Site owners are responsible for any required visitor notices or consent.

Google Analytics | Google Terms of Service | Google Privacy Policy

Google Maps

When an administrator configures a Maps API key and adds a Local SEO map shortcode, pages with that shortcode load the Maps JavaScript API from maps.googleapis.com. The visitor’s browser sends the API key, IP address, browser information, and map requests, including configured location coordinates, to Google.

Google Maps JavaScript API | Google Maps Platform Terms | Google Privacy Policy

Administrator-requested URL retrieval

Schema import and live schema validation retrieve the URL an administrator chooses when using either tool. The WordPress server sends the request directly to that URL. The remote operator’s terms and privacy practices depend on the chosen URL.

SEO Analyzer and sitemap self-checks

When an administrator runs the SEO Analyzer, the WordPress server requests its own public homepage, sitemaps, robots.txt, RSS feed, and HTTP/HTTPS or www/non-www URL variants. The authorized sitemap connector can also request the site’s public sitemap. These requests contain standard HTTP headers and expose the server IP address to infrastructure handling those URLs, such as the site’s host or CDN.

Development

The distributed plugin includes readable block source and build manifests. The FAQ, HowTo, and Quick Answer block sources are in blocks/faq/src/, blocks/howto/src/, and blocks/quick-answer/src/. The compiled bundles are under build/blocks/.

From a source checkout with package.json and package-lock.json, rebuild the bundles with:

npm ci
npm run build
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New and search for SEOvault AI.
  2. Install and activate the plugin.
  3. Open SEOvault AI in the admin menu and follow the setup steps.

For security, run WordPress on a supported PHP version with the latest security patches from your host.
sections.faq:
Do I need an SEOvault AI account?

You can use the free WordPress SEO features without an account. An account is needed to use the optional SEOvault AI web app.

Can I import my existing SEO settings?

You can import supported SEO data from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, SiteSEO, Slim SEO, SureRank, Squirrly SEO, and The SEO Framework.

How do I switch without duplicating SEO output?

Import your existing data and spot-check a few pages. Once you are ready to switch, use one primary SEO plugin to avoid duplicate metadata, schema, and sitemaps.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Updated user-facing naming to consistently use “SEOvault AI” across importer messages, schema guidance, block descriptions, and admin notices.
  • Some formatting cleanup.

1.2.0

  • Added configurable Organization identity schema fields and publishing-policy references.
  • Added Local SEO extension hooks for custom map markers, organization logos, and KML placemark data.
  • Added Webmaster Verification controls, verification-code export, 404-log CSV export, and more schema types.
  • Added automatic keyword suggestions, schema-dialog improvements, and clearer generated-value status indicators.
  • Redesigned the dashboard status and attention views and refined its responsive WordPress-native interface.
  • Added link-schema infrastructure, improved redirect workflows, and prevented KML sitemap header errors.
  • Added WordPress 7.1 editor-canvas compatibility and strengthened request, output, connector-auth, and packaging boundaries carried forward from the approved 1.1.2 release.

For the complete release history, visit the SEOvault AI changelog.
